issue.body: ## What Changed - Records each completed agent turn as a file-level change set using T3 Code's existing checkpoint refs and durable activity stream. - Adds a Provenance panel for reviewing changed files, the producing turn, provider, and recorded line ranges. - Previews and applies selective code undo for one turn while preserving compatible work added afterward. - Surfaces shared-checkout overlap, unattributed dirty-file changes, worktree mismatch, and recovery failures above the composer. - Opens the relevant checkpoint diff and conversation directly from provenance controls. - Adds integration guidance for deciding which parallel turns can combine independently and which require review. ## Why A full checkpoint rewind can erase valid work that happened after one bad agent turn. Provenance lets users identify the responsible turn, inspect its checkpoint patch, and remove only that turn when Git proves the reverse patch still applies cleanly. ## Safety Details - Provenance is opt-in with `T3_PROVENANCE_ENABLED=1` while the workflow is evaluated. - Selective undo derives a context-anchored patch from the target turn's before and after checkpoint refs, preventing stale offsets or duplicate lines from being reversed accidentally. - Git checks the complete reverse patch against the live workspace before applying it. A conflicting multi-file patch is refused without partially modifying files. - Binary changes and renames remain review-only. - Later compatible edits and conversation history remain intact; nearby ambiguous edits are conservatively sent to manual review. - Successful undo writes a durable receipt containing the affected paths and patch SHA-256. - Turn summaries reuse the provider's existing final response. Provenance makes no additional model calls and adds no system-prompt content or provider tokens. ## Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1017acee-abc9-4c90-9fa9-831013b189eb ## UI ### Safe Undo attached to the composer ### Expanded recovery scope and turn provenance ## Testing 1. Start T3 Code with `T3_PROVENANCE_ENABLED=1`. 2. Run one turn that changes two files. 3. Run a later turn that changes a separate region in one of those files. 4. Open **Provenance**, select the earlier turn, and preview recovery. 5. Confirm the target patch is marked for removal and the compatible later change is preserved. 6. Apply the undo, then inspect the workspace diff and durable recovery receipt. 7. Modify the same target lines and retry; confirm the undo is refused and no file is partially changed. ## Verification - `vp run --filter @t3tools/client-runtime typecheck` - `vp run --filter t3 typecheck` - `vp run --filter @t3tools/web typecheck` - `node scripts/provenance-smoke-test.mjs` - `node --test scripts/provenance-undo.test.mjs` (8 real-Git recovery scenarios) - Focused checkpoint regression: exact 25,000-line provenance summaries - `git diff --check` - Manual validation covered attribution, conversation navigation, overlap alerts, recovery preview, prior-turn selection, and selective undo. ## Checklist - [x] Reuses T3 Code's checkpoint and activity architecture - [x] Makes no additional provider calls or prompt changes - [x] Refuses unsupported or conflicting recovery patches - [x] Preserves compatible later work in the Git-backed smoke test - [x] Includes one demo and two focused UI screenshots - [x] Documents the opt-in rollout flag Generated with GPT-5 and GPT-6 in OpenAI Codex desktop using the Codex harness. > [!NOTE] > ### Add thread provenance tracking and selective agent rollback > - Records per-file mutations, line ranges, and historical overlaps in `CheckpointReactor` to track agent changes. > - Adds `SafeHistoryPanel` and `SafeIntegrationPanel` to search, review, and classify turn changes by safe-undo readiness. > - Introduces UI banners, turn review cards, and a conflict review layout for provenance overlaps and workspace mismatches. > - Implements selective undo via reverse-patch validation and a new `provenance-turn` scope in the checkpoint revert command schema. > - Behavioral Change: Provenance is disabled by default and requires `T3_PROVENANCE_ENABLED=1`. Provider turns are now blocked before execution if the thread workspace path differs from the provider session cwd. > > > > Macroscope summarized 1e201e3. > >
